authority.meaning: A successful system or library call may leave a nonzero errno. Its error meaning applies immediately after a failing return, not a successful open.
authority.title: Perl predefined variables: $!

falsification: Compare the original and corrected verifier on the same valid short-read case; require the original to reject and successor to accept. Add rejection controls for missing open success, wrong flags, and malformed errno. Existing reader/descriptor/effect falsifiers stay active.
limits: This diagnoses an incorrect oracle assumption; it does not attribute the internal source of errno 25 to a particular libc or PerlIO operation. Successful errno is retained evidence, not an error signal. All other original audit checks remain in force.
mechanism: The first independent audit wrongly required errno zero after successful CORE sysopen. The unchanged reader and real descriptor succeeded; the hook captured errno 25 immediately after CORE sysopen. All selected current opens and the eight separately qualified historical reader opens carry this successful nonzero errno.
repair: Preserve the original audit and 31 producer pins unchanged. A separately pinned successor requires exact successful open arity/flags/return and a numeric captured errno, while retaining exact failed-read errno, diagnostics, bytes, descriptor identity and closure checks. Re-audit the same immutable cases; never rerun the qualifier.
